quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (annual securities report, IFRS): revenue JPY 884,638 million (+23.7%; JPY 714,940 million the year before) and operating profit JPY 174,967 million (JPY 112,484 million); profit before tax JPY 169,082 million. Management attributes the growth to higher sales of its main products, semiconductor sputtering targets and rolled copper foil, and a higher copper price, despite a stronger yen (average JPY 151 per US dollar; LME copper averaged 491 cents per pound and hit a then-record 628 cents on January 29, 2026). Segments: Semiconductor Materials sales JPY 177,195 million (119.7% of the prior year), segment profit JPY 39,492 million (JPY 26,738 million); ICT Materials sales JPY 318,744 million (120.2%), segment profit JPY 31,477 million (JPY 25,085 million); Basic Materials sales JPY 407,877 million (133.1%), segment profit JPY 139,465 million (JPY 74,517 million), on higher copper prices and higher equity-method income from Caserones operator MLCC, which recognised deferred tax assets. In Metals & Recycling, management is considering production cuts at the group's smelter because copper-concentrate purchase terms have deteriorated sharply.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 884,638 million (+23.7%); operating profit JPY 174,967 million; Semiconductor Materials sales JPY 177,195 million (119.7%), segment profit JPY 39,492 million

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor Materials, year ended March 2026 (annual securities report): management states AI-related demand kept growing and demand for advanced logic semiconductors and memory stayed at a high level on needs for large-capacity data storage and faster data communication, lifting sales of semiconductor sputtering targets and its other main products. Segment external sales by customer location: Taiwan JPY 47,656 million (JPY 44,652 million the year before), the US JPY 36,754 million (JPY 26,543 million), other Asia JPY 34,522 million (JPY 28,564 million), Japan JPY 28,821 million (JPY 19,615 million), other regions JPY 15,757 million (JPY 14,950 million), China JPY 13,055 million (JPY 13,104 million). ICT Materials grew on rolled copper foil sales as smartphone demand recovered and on wider adoption of its high-performance copper alloys, led by titanium copper, in AI servers.

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management's view (annual securities report): the semiconductor logic and memory market keeps growing on the rapid spread of generative AI; because leading-edge logic has more wiring layers and uses more sputtering targets, management expects its sputtering-target sales volume to grow faster than the logic and memory market, while ever finer wiring is raising needs for CVD/ALD thin-film deposition. AI servers use many of its Semiconductor Materials products - sputtering targets for on-chip wiring, InP substrates for optical communications, high-purity tantalum powder for tantalum capacitors and magnetic-material targets for high-capacity HDDs - and management also expects target demand to grow in packaging (inter-chip wiring such as TSV and RDL, and chiplet interconnects). In ICT Materials, adoption of titanium copper in AI-server connectors is expanding rapidly and demand for leak sensors that detect coolant leaks inside AI servers is expected to grow. Priorities: expand capacity and productivity for data-center and AI-server products (semiconductor sputtering targets, magnetic-material sputtering targets, InP substrates, tantalum powder, titanium copper), and create next-generation global top-share products in advanced materials and advanced packaging (the JOINT3 next-generation packaging consortium, CVD/ALD materials, CdZnTe substrates for medical and sensor uses).

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The company opened the Hitachinaka plant (Ibaraki) on March 26, 2026 as a new core site for advanced materials, starting with semiconductors: anticipating demand growth in advanced logic and advanced memory (HBM and others) mainly for AI data centers, it is to strengthen supply of semiconductor sputtering targets and other products and host R&D and new-business creation (annual securities report). Capital expenditure in the year ended March 2026 was JPY 77,904 million: Semiconductor Materials JPY 24,313 million (capacity expansion for thin-film / semiconductor target products - added production equipment at the Isohara site, equipment at the Mesa plant in Arizona, building and equipment at the Hitachinaka site), ICT Materials JPY 27,920 million (rolled copper foil equipment at the Hitachi site, maintenance at the Kurami plant), Basic Materials JPY 17,002 million (maintenance at the Saganoseki smelter) and common JPY 8,669 million (Hitachinaka infrastructure, new-business R&D).
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 77,904 million; Semiconductor Materials capex JPY 24,313 million

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Planned major facilities (annual securities report; the added capacity is not stated): semiconductor-materials manufacturing equipment at the Hitachinaka site, JPY 25,700 million (JPY 9,346 million paid; October 2024 to March 2026), and a further JPY 23,110 million project there (October 2026 to September 2028); indium phosphide (InP) substrate manufacturing equipment at the Isohara site in four projects - JPY 1,500 million (July 2025 to January 2027), JPY 3,898 million (October 2025 to August 2027), JPY 1,918 million (December 2025 to January 2028) and JPY 18,010 million (April 2026 to August 2030); nickel powder manufacturing equipment at Toho Titanium's Wakamatsu plant, JPY 10,649 million (JPY 9,725 million paid; September 2023 to September 2026); new-product manufacturing equipment at the Hitachi and Hitachinaka sites, JPY 13,224 million (JPY 2,546 million paid; July 2024 to March 2030); shared utilities for the new Hitachinaka plant, JPY 47,240 million (JPY 13,711 million paid; March 2022 to April 2029). No significant disposals are planned.

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual securities report): group R&D spending was JPY 19,983 million in the year ended March 2026 - Semiconductor Materials JPY 6,007 million, ICT Materials JPY 5,180 million, Basic Materials JPY 1,213 million, new businesses and other JPY 7,583 million. Semiconductor Materials is improving the quality of sputtering targets used in advanced processes for generative AI and developing targets for new needs in advanced packaging; for InP substrates used in optical communication devices inside AI data centers it is focused on development for larger diameters. ICT Materials is developing new titanium- and Corson-type copper alloys for semiconductor lead frames and camera-module springs, and rolled copper foil for robots and 5G/6G. CVD/ALD materials: after setting up a CVD/ALD materials business office in February 2024, the company built a mass-production line for new high-purity CVD/ALD materials and shipped samples that won good customer evaluations; expecting rapid demand growth from full adoption, it decided to raise capacity - the expansion at Toho Titanium's Chigasaki plant is complete and running at full operation, and a mass-production line in the Hitachi area of the Ibaraki works has started up and begun shipping to customers. In September 2025 it joined JOINT3, the next-generation semiconductor packaging consortium set up by Resonac.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 19,983 million; Semiconductor Materials R&D JPY 6,007 million

quarterly_data.quarter: JX Advanced Metals annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Material contracts (annual securities report): under share-exchange and business-integration agreements signed February 25, 2026, Toho Titanium - 50.37% owned at fiscal year-end and a listed subsidiary - became a wholly owned subsidiary on June 1, 2026, the effective date of the share exchange. On March 10, 2026 the company agreed to sell 5% of SCM Minera Lumina Copper Chile (operator of the Caserones copper mine) to LMC Caserones SpA, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lundin Mining Corporation, cutting its stake to 25% while keeping its preferential offtake rights to Caserones copper concentrate and copper cathode at the same proportion as before.
